# Exotic Quirks Table

*Pages PDF 10-11*

## **Exotic Quirks Table**
| 2d10 | Exotic Quirk |
|---|---|
| 2 | occasion, a wealthy landlord may even keep an Ogre on as a Doorman, although this is a risky proposition as Ogres are not subtle in their understanding of the finer principles of enforcement, cost a fortune in fresh meat by way of payment, often abandon their posts without warning due to a fit of wanderlust, and may kill and eat another guest. Elf Guests.  A group of two to four Elves. These will most likely be High Elf envoys on a trade mission or matter of political importance. Even if they are at a high class establishment, they will be dismayed at the crudeness and grime |
| 3 | of a Human tavern, as well as the lack of sophistication to the fare and entertainment therein. They will be behave with an attitude of benign patronage, or extreme condescension, to any Humans they interact with. The Elves will be pleased to move on as soon as they can, probably to the relief of everyone else in the tavern. Haunted.  One of the bedrooms is haunted by a Ghost. Mostly it is restful, but there is a 3% chance on any given |
| 4 | night that it manifests and attacks a guest. These attacks last 1d10 Rounds, after which the Ghost becomes docile. Unconventional Beliefs.  Landlord holds extreme religious views and only employs people who do not offend them. |
| 5 | Most likely they are a strict Sigmarite with a prejudice against Ulricans but may be a strict Ulrican with a dislike of Sigmarites. They may hold sympathies with a fanatical or heretical sect, or even worship a proscribed deity. Pit Fight.  The tavern may be the venue for a clandestine pit fight. If so, this will hidden in the bowels of the cellars, |
| 6 | or in a suitably private outbuilding. The contestants may be Human, but could include captured Goblins, Giant Spiders, Beastmen, or other creatures. Unlicensed Magic User.  One of the tavern’s customers is a Witch. Their abilities are left to the GM, but they should |
| 7 | at least have the Channelling and Language (Magick) skills of 35+4d10, 4 Petty Spells, and 4 Spells from the Lore of Witchcraft.  Challenging (+0) Gossip  (see Quality of Gossip on page 18). Hex.  One of the bedrooms carries the germ of a curse. Maybe there is an unquiet spirit here, or a previous occupant |
| 8 | offended the Spites. Should anyone spend the night here, they must take a  Challenging (+0) Cool  Test. Those that fail suffer horrifying nightmares and lose all remaining Fortune points for the remainder of the session. Altered Punter. |
| 9 | One of the customers or members of staff at the tavern harbours a mutation. Whilst they haven’t yet fallen to Chaos, they are on a path to corruption. Giant Rats. |
| 10 | The cellar is infested with Giant Rats. Whilst they shy away from contact with Characters, they defend themselves if cornered and may transmit Ratte Fever. Dwarf Guests.  A group of three to six Dwarfs. They may be labourers on a local building site (Brass Tier), Engineers planning a new project (Silver Tier), or Merchants looking to set up a new trade route (Gold Tier). For the most 11 part, they will keep to themselves, but anyone who impresses them (usually through demonstrating the ability to pass four consecutive Consome Alcohol Tests) will be treated with gruff but sincere respect. Plague Carrier.  One of the guests carries the Black Plague, Itching Pox, or similar contagious disease. Whilst this |
| 12 | person may not currently be exhibiting symptoms, they could still pass the illness on to anyone they come into contact with. Blue Mould.  A patch of Blue Mould is growing underneath one of the beds in the tavern. It will be triggered if the |
| 13 | bed is shifted or rocked violently. If triggered, the mould releases a cloud of spores for 5 yards around the bed. The cloud lasts for 1d10 Rounds. Characters in the area must pass an  Average (+20) Endurance  Test or gain 1  Poisoned Condition, plus a further 1  Poisoned  Condition per –SL. Yellow Mould.  A patch of Yellow Mould is growing in a forgotten part of the cellars. Characters who enter the area can avoid triggering the mould on a  Difficult (–10) Stealth  Test. If triggered, the mould releases a cloud of spores |
| 14 | for 5 yards to either side of the patch. The cloud lasts for 1d10 Rounds. Characters in the area must pass an  Average (+20) Endurance  Test or gain 1  Blinded  condition, plus a further 1  Blinded  condition per –SL. Also, all Characters receive 1 Wound for every Round spent in the cloud. |

| 2d10 | Exotic Quirk |
|---|---|
| 15 | The attic is home to a Giant Spider. It crept in as a tiny juvenile but has grown on a steady diet of rats, birds, and beetles. It is now Size Small and getting hungrier. Should anyone come up, it will attack them. Magic Artefact.  The tavern is home to a magical item of some sort. This may be a possession of a member of staff |
| 16 | who understands its properties and guards it jealously, or it may lie neglected amongst a jumble of mundane tools and cutlery, or even used as a wall decoration. Warpstone.  A shard of warpstone has been left on the grounds of the tavern by a previous visitor, either stashed 17 by someone planning to return for it or left as a deliberate corrupting influence. Cache of Dreamwine.  Among the bottles in the wine cellar is a crate of unmarked bottles, containing a thick, |
| 18 | dark wine. This is Dreamwine, which can have catastrophic effects on regular drinkers. See  Altdorf: Crown of the Empire  or  Winds of Magic  for more details. Snotlings.  A band of 1d10 Snotlings have infested a neglected corner of the cellars. They are terrified of the Humans that occasionally come here to leave or retrieve barrels of ale and have so far hidden successfully. At 19 night, they creep out to steal food and shiny items from the kitchen and common room, and the smell of their ordure permeates the establishment. If they are confronted, they cannot be reasoned with and fight for their lives. Vampire.  One of the guests at the tavern is secretly a Vampire. It may be travelling alone, or in the company of three Human servants. It may display a clue as to its nature, such as avoiding proximity to a religous symbol, being inactive during the hours of daylight, and refusing to eat food or drink wine. During the night, there is a 50% chance that the Vampire will attempt to drink the blood of another guest. It will attempt to prey upon a sleeping guest by making an  Opposed Stealth/Percepetion  Test. If this is passed, the Vampire drinks the sleeper’s blood, inflicting 1d10 Wounds in the process. The victim is not woken, but will feel weak in the morning, with bruised and broken skin at the site of the bite and a  Fatigued Surprised |
| 20 | Condition. If the victim wakes, they will suffer a Condition, and the Vampire will attempt to place them in a grapple. If the Vampire succeeds in grappling them in the initial Round of combat, it will bite them and drain blood as described before they can raise the alarm. The Vampire will then attempt to escape or disable its victim through the use of magic. If the Vampire is confident that it can get away with its blood drinking, it will not necessarily kill its victim, but will have no qualms about doing so if it feels it is likely to meet stiff resistance. If things start to go against the Vampire, it will attempt to flee, and any Human servants accompanying the Vampire will fight to the death in order to protect the creature and ensure its escape. |
